A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, and Appendices A-C support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and KuaiRec-based simulation results for welfare, population dynamics, regret, and dynamics estimation in Sections 6-7 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original synthetic and KuaiRec-based simulation results, including the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The population model, look-ahead objective, softmax approximation, interpolation rule, and dynamics-estimation procedure remain unchanged in Sections 2 and 5 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic environment and KuaiRec-based recommendation simulation. Appendix C's new fixed-population example is explanatory, not an additional evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Both compare the same interpolation settings, including myopic-greedy and pure look-ahead policies, against uniform random allocation. Newly cited research is not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain 20 viewer and provider groups, the same small and large initializations, 200 simulation timesteps, and 100 gradient iterations. KuaiRec preprocessing, dynamics noise, burn-in, and evaluation metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: The interpolation sensitivity, initialization comparisons, utility heatmaps, and true-versus-estimated dynamics analyses are retained. Figure 2 already contains both initialization conditions in v1; v2 only clarifies its caption.

E5.justification: Averaging over 10 provider permutations and the plotted uncertainty remain unchanged. Neither version adds experimental seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence-interval procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The result curves and heatmaps in Figures 1-8 are unchanged, as are the reported findings, including the best KuaiRec interpolation value of beta = 0.6. Figure 6 changes panel-title terminology only.

T1.justification: Appendix B replaces v1's eventual distance-monotonicity definition of a fixed point with lambda_eq = S(lambda_eq). It adds a separate epsilon-delta stability definition and a determinant-based sufficient-condition assertion. The substantive theorem statements, derivations, and proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The conclusion changes the algorithm's claimed guarantee of viewer satisfaction and provider exposure into an empirical demonstration. The introduction similarly softens exposure-guaranteeing policies from being useful to potentially useful; the central contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly explains how spreading exposure too thinly with a fixed viewer population can make concentration preferable. Section 3.1 expands the equilibrium interpretation, and the new Impact Statement discusses broader potential applications.

D1.justification: v2's abstract adds an experiment-code availability statement and repository pointer, absent from v1. Other implementation and experimental details remain unchanged; repository availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: Sections 3.1 and 8 expand comparisons with one-sided market equilibria and performative prediction. New references include Narang et al., Mazumdar et al., and two additional Yao et al. papers, while the central population-growth positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections, expands explanatory paragraphs, adds an Impact Statement, and updates publication and correspondence information. The main section sequence and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout, extensively reflowing text and figures. Appendix figures are redistributed, Figure 2's misleading appendix reference is corrected, Figure 5's caption is repaired, and Figure 6 replaces 'user' with 'viewer' in panel titles.

improvement.justification: v2 improves captions, qualifies exposure-allocation claims, corrects the fixed-point definition, and adds code-access information. However, its new Definition 2 incorrectly treats det(∇λS) < 1 as sufficient for stability: even Appendix B.2's example can satisfy this while having an eigenvalue above one. These clarity and documentation gains coexist with a new mathematical misstatement in a central theoretical concept, preventing a confident net-quality judgment.
